reason: E3 directly supports elastic undulations as precursors to twinning in a HEA, but only under monotonic loading, not sustained creep. No cited evidence addresses interface undulations in nanoscale multilayers, stress localisation by such undulations, or their role in lowering dislocation nucleation barriers under creep. The remaining evidence concerns general HEA plasticity, not the specific multilayer creep mechanism proposed.
premises: Sustained loading triggers nonlinear elastic instabilities at multilayer interfaces forming nanoscale undulations
These undulations localize stress and lower the barrier for dislocation nucleation
The coupled dislocation/twinning activity drives progressive plastic deformation while preserving strength and ductility
The mechanism dominates when diffusion creep is not favoured
